families.title: Deleting parts of the owner aggregate

tasks.prompt: Add a way to delete a single visit: `POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/delete` must delete that visit from the database and redirect to `/owners/{ownerId}`. All other visits and pets must stay unchanged. No UI changes are required. Make sure the project's build and tests still pass.

Add a way to delete a pet: `POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/delete` must delete the pet and all of its visits from the database and redirect to `/owners/{ownerId}`. The owner's other pets and their visits must stay unchanged. No UI changes are required. Make sure the project's build and tests still pass.

Add a way to purge old visits of a pet: `POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/purge` with the request parameter `before` (an ISO date, `yyyy-MM-dd`) must delete from the database every visit of that pet dated strictly before `before`, and redirect to `/owners/{ownerId}`. Visits on or after that date and the visits of other pets must stay unchanged. No UI changes are required. Make sure the project's build and tests still pass.

The owner search (`GET /owners`) should also filter by city: an optional request parameter `city` restricts the results to owners whose city is exactly that value, combined with the existing last-name search; a missing or empty `city` means no city filter. Add a City input (request parameter `city`) to the Find Owners form. When the results span several pages, every pagination link on the owner list must keep the active search parameters (`lastName` and `city`). Existing behavior stays: a single match redirects to that owner's page, no match shows the Find Owners form again. Make sure the project's build and tests still pass.

The veterinarians page (`GET /vets.html`) should support filtering by specialty: an optional request parameter `specialty` (a specialty name, e.g. `radiology`) restricts the list to vets having that specialty; a missing or empty `specialty` means no filter. Paging stays as it is (5 vets per page), and every pagination link on the page must keep the active `specialty` filter. No other UI changes are required. Make sure the project's build and tests still pass.

The owner search (`GET /owners`) should also filter by pet type: an optional request parameter `petType` (a pet type name, e.g. `hamster`) restricts the results to owners who have at least one pet of that type, combined with the existing last-name search; every matching owner appears only once; a missing or empty `petType` means no pet type filter. Add a pet type input (request parameter `petType`) to the Find Owners form. When the results span several pages, every pagination link on the owner list must keep the active search parameters (`lastName` and `petType`). Existing behavior stays: a single match redirects to that owner's page, no match shows the Find Owners form again. Make sure the project's build and tests still pass.
